change_summary: Decider self-applied ISS-2538 (major): duplicate paragraph in detail_evidence removed. Verifying patch landed cleanly and no new holes introduced.
our_argument_summary: 1-2 nT lunar magnetic signal is generated by ocean tidal dynamo (seawater moving through Earth's magnetic field), first detected by CHAMP (Tyler et al. 2003) and refined by Swarm (Sabaka et al. 2015). Globe model predicts magnitude, spatial pattern, and phase from first principles. Dome has no ocean induction mechanism. Dome's W015 prediction (-1.0 nT) disagrees in sign with claimed confirmation (+1-2 nT). Measurement published over 20 years before dome claimed it.

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: No live monitoring. The dome's prediction file 03-predictions.txt explicitly records W015 as 'Lunar phase magnetic -1.0 nT +/-0.5 -> 1-2 nT confirmed -> WIN-039', surfacing the sign contradiction directly in the dome's own source: predicted -1.0 nT, 'confirmed' +1-2 nT. No monitor.py or pull_data.py present in raw-text/ for this WIN — the automation either never tracked this signal or was removed.
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: Hardcoded — predicted and observed values are static text in the predictions file; no computation.
dome_code_analysis.escape_clauses: None; the tolerance band (-1.0 +/-0.5 -> [-1.5, -0.5] nT) does NOT include +1-2 nT, so the dome's own tolerance arithmetic rejects this as a confirmation. The dome simply asserts 'confirmed' anyway.
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: None. Our detail_evidence accurately captures the W015 sign mismatch.

code_analysis_tags.monitoring_evidence: No monitor.py routine present for W015. The predictions file is static text; no API fetch, no comparison logic. Matches c3 tag.
code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Standard EM induction (Tyler 2003, Sabaka 2015) explains the signal from seawater conductivity × tidal velocity × Earth's B-field. The dome adopts the magnitude without offering an alternative derivation — it relabels the signal as 'aetheric' without disputing the standard mechanism's predictions.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: Tyler et al. published in Science (2003) and Sabaka et al. refined with Swarm (2015) — both decades before the dome's WIN-039 entry. Acknowledged in current detail_evidence.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: No derivation from dome geometry (disc radius, firmament height, moon altitude 2,534 km) to the magnitude 1-2 nT. The dome's own predicted value (-1.0 nT) lacks a derivation path and contradicts the adopted observation in sign.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome author is correct that the lunar magnetic signal exists and is ~1-2 nT — the empirical phenomenon is real (wins.json:WIN-039.detail_evidence cites Tyler 2003 and Sabaka 2015). The dome's instinct that there is a real lunar-correlated geomagnetic signal worth pointing at is not wrong.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The dome's own W015 prediction file (raw-text/03-predictions.txt:W015) predicted -1.0 nT +/-0.5 — a negative excursion outside the tolerance band that would include the observed +1 to +2 nT positive enhancement. By the dome's own arithmetic this is not a confirmation, yet 'confirmed' is asserted anyway. Additionally, no derivation from dome geometry (disc_radius, firmament_height, moon altitude 2,534 km per CLAUDE.md) produces 1-2 nT — the magnitude is borrowed from Tyler 2003 (wins.json:WIN-039.detail_verdict_text). Combined: the kernel-of-truth (signal exists) doesn't survive the dome's own self-contradiction (sign error) or the post-hoc test (Part 3.1b standard, cited in detail_verdict_text).

deeper_analysis:
Verification scope: confirm ISS-2538 patch closed the duplicate paragraph cleanly and surface any new holes. Outcome: patch landed, no substantive new holes. The surviving paragraph carries the same argument (globe model predicts spatial pattern, dome cannot) but now states it once. Sign-mismatch and post-hoc paragraphs preserved.

OTHER SIDE: A dome defender could argue the curmudgeon's c3 'major' grading of an editorial duplicate was overzealous — duplications happen, they don't change the science. Defensible response: the dome project's own credibility critique rests on editorial rigor; presenting the same paragraph twice on the published site IS the kind of error we flag in dome content. Major grading was appropriate.

Three carry-over holes (ISS-2539/2540/2541) remain open. The decider chose to address them in separate runs rather than bundle them into one patch — this is fine; ISS-2539 (discriminatory-test framing) needs careful prose work, ISS-2540 (DOIs) is mechanical, ISS-2541 (TLDR omits sign discrepancy) is a TLDR rewrite. Each will get its own push.
